transcript.text: fridge part freezin stuff, lettuce + yoghurts frozen solid at the back. hotpoint ff. any ideas pls

That sounds like a classic defrost system fault. On frost-free fridge-freezers, if the automatic defrost cycle fails, ice builds up on the evaporator coils at the back of the freezer. This blocks the cold air from flowing into the fridge compartment, causing items near the back wall (like your lettuce and yoghurts) to freeze solid while the rest of the fridge may be too warm. Before we look for a faulty part, please do these two quick checks:
1. Check the door seals: Run your fingers around the rubber gaskets on both doors. Are they torn, loose, or dirty? A bad seal lets in warm air and causes excess ice.
2. Manual Defrost: Switch the appliance off at the wall socket, remove all food (keep it cold), and leave the doors open for 24–48 hours until all ice has melted. Dry everything thoroughly. Once you've done that, switch it back on. If the freezing problem returns after a few days, we likely have a failed defrost heater or thermostat that needs replacing.
seals look fine. freezer food is solid as normal tho. do i really need to empty it all out for 48hrs? its really full after big shop

You don't need to empty everything if you can do a partial defrost. Since the freezer is still cold and working normally, the issue is likely that ice has built up on the evaporator coils (usually behind a panel at the back of the freezer) and is blocking the cold air from circulating into the fridge section. To confirm this without emptying the whole thing:
1. Unplug the appliance.
2. Remove only the items near the back wall or any shelves that block access to the rear panel in the freezer.
3. Leave the doors open for a few hours (or overnight) until you see if there is ice melting on the coils behind the panel. If you find a solid block of ice, that suggests a defrost fault (likely the heater or thermostat). If it looks clear and just cold, we need to look at whether food is blocking the air vents inside the fridge compartment. Can you tell me if there is visible ice on the back wall/coils in the freezer?
not looked in the freezer back, haven't unplugged anything yet. fridge is rammed tho, stuff is pressed right against the vent slots at the back. dial is on max too, kids might have moved it

That dial setting is very likely the main culprit here. If it's on 'Max', the fridge compartment can easily drop below zero degrees, especially if food is pressed right up against the cold back wall where the air comes out. This is a free fix and doesn't require unplugging anything. Please do this:
1. Turn the dial to a mid-range setting (often marked as 3 or 'Normal').
2. Move all items, especially the lettuce and yoghurts, at least 2-3cm away from the back wall so air can circulate.
3. Leave it for about 12 hours with the doors shut. Check if the food is still freezing solid after that time. If they are fine now, you just had a setting issue and over-packing. If they are still frozen solid despite being moved away from the wall and the dial being normal, then we likely have an internal ice block on the evaporator coils (a defrost fault), which would require a manual defrost to clear temporarily.
did that, dial on middle and cleared the vents. after 2 days its better but one yoghurt right at the very back still froze. is that normal?

It is not strictly 'normal' for food to freeze solid, but it is very common in the first few days after moving a dial from Max to Normal. The fridge needs time to stabilise its temperature and airflow. You likely just had a combination of an over-cold setting and blocked vents. However, because one item still froze at the very back, we need to make sure there isn't a small blockage or a slight defrost issue lingering. 1. Ensure nothing is touching the back wall or blocking the vent slots (usually located between the fridge and freezer shelves or at the top rear of the fridge section).
2. Place your hand near those vents to confirm you feel cold air circulating freely into the fridge compartment.
3. If the airflow feels strong but that specific spot is still freezing, it may be a 'cold spot' caused by how items are stacked (e.g., dense items like yoghurt pots conduct cold faster). Try moving that item slightly forward or wrapping it in a tea towel to see if it thaws out. If the airflow feels weak or blocked, or if more items start freezing despite being moved away from the wall, we likely have a defrost system fault (like a faulty heater or thermostat) causing ice to build up behind that back panel. In that case, you would need to unplug it for 24 hours to clear the ice completely.
ok will move it forward a bit. dont think i can feel the airflow properly tho. if it's just the odd yoghurt at the very back is that fine to leave?

It is not strictly 'fine' to leave it if food keeps freezing, but one isolated yoghurt pot can often be managed by moving it slightly forward. The most reliable way to tell if this is a simple 'overpacking' issue or a broken part (defrost heater/thermostat) is to do a full manual defrost. Please unplug the appliance for 24 hours with both doors open (keep food cold in bags/towels). Once done, dry it out and plug it back in. If the fridge cools normally without freezing things after this reset, we have confirmed a defrost system fault that needs a part replacement. If you prefer not to do a full 24-hour defrost right now, just ensure nothing is touching the back wall and monitor if more items freeze over the next few days.
